Key Points

\n\n
    \n\t
  • Diagonal pitch in a Full Lap joint is a calculated parameter.
    • \n\t
  • The formula for diagonal pitch is pd = (2p+d)3(2p+d)3\n\t\n\t, where:
    • \n\t
  • p is the pitch of rivets.
    • \n\t
  • d is the diameter of rivets.
    • \n\t
  • This formula ensures proper rivet spacing and joint strength.
    • \n\t
  • Correct diagonal pitch minimizes stress concentration and improves load distribution.
    • \n
\n\n

    \n\t

      \n\t\t
    • Rivet joints are widely used in structural applications.
      • \n\t\t
    • They provide a secure connection for overlapping plates.
      • \n\t
    \n\t
    • \n\t
  • Lap Joint:\n\t
      \n\t\t
    • A lap joint involves overlapping two plates and fastening them using rivets.
      • \n\t\t
    • Full Lap joints are commonly used in engineering applications for their strength.
      • \n\t

    Key Points

    \n\n
      \n\t
    • The same basic size is specified for both the shaft and the hole when used for fits.
      • \n\t
    • This ensures a precise and standardized fit between the two components.
      • \n\t
    • It is a critical factor in the design and manufacturing of mechanical parts for proper functioning.
      • \n\t
    • Adopting the same basic size minimizes errors and misalignment in the assembly process.
      • \n\t
    • It helps in achieving interchangeability of parts in production and maintenance.
      • \n
    \n\n

    Additional Information

    \n\n
      \n\t
    • Clearance Fit:\n\n\t
        \n\t\t
      • In a clearance fit, the hole is always larger than the shaft, ensuring free movement.
        • \n\t\t
      • This type of fit is commonly used in applications where relative motion is required.
        • \n\t
      \n\t
      • \n\t
    • Interference Fit:\n\t
        \n\t\t
      • In an interference fit, the shaft is slightly larger than the hole, creating a tight assembly.
        • \n\t\t
      • This type of fit is used for applications requiring a fixed and secure connection.
        • \n\t
      \n\t
      • \n\t
    • Transition Fit:\n\t
        \n\t\t
      • A transition fit may result in either a clearance or an interference, depending on the tolerances.
        • \n\t\t
      • It is used in applications requiring both precision and flexibility.
        • \n\t
      \n\t
      • \n

      \n\n
        \n\t
      • To construct a rectangle, the length of two adjacent sides is sufficient.
        • \n\t
      • A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles.
        • \n\t
      • The dimensions of a rectangle are defined by the lengths of its two adjacent sides.
        • \n\t
      • Once the lengths of adjacent sides are known, the opposite sides are equal in length, ensuring the rectangle's shape.

      • The diagonal can be calculated using the Pythagorean theorem if needed.

          \n\t\t

          \n\t\t

        Key Points

        • Article 24 of the Indian Constitution prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, and other hazardous employment.
          • \n\t
        • It aims to safeguard children from exploitation and ensure their right to education and a safe childhood.
          • \n\t
        • This provision is a part of Fundamental Rights under the Indian Constitution, ensuring the protection of children.
          • \n\t
        • It is in line with international conventions such as the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC).
          • \n\t
        • Further, the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act strictly enforces this prohibition with additional guidelines.
          • \n\t
        • The goal is to eliminate child labour in hazardous environments and encourage universal education.

        \n\n
          \n\t

            \n\t\t
          • The Act prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in certain occupations and processes.
            • \n\t\t

          • It complements Article 24 to eradicate child labour and promote education.

        • शिक्षा का अधिकार:\n\t

          • शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009, 6-14 वर्ष की आयु के बच्चों के लिए शिक्षा सुनिश्चित करता है।
            • \n\t\t
          • यह बाल श्रम को खत्म करने और शिक्षा को बढ़ावा देने के लिए अनुच्छेद 24 का पूरक है।

        \n\nc8:T541,

        Given:

        \n\n

        A can do the work in 14 hours

        \n\n

        B can do the work in 21 hours

        \n\n

        Total time = 10 hours

        \n\n

        Formula used:

        \n\n

        Work = LCM of individual times

        \n\n

        Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

        \n\n

        Calculations:

        \n\n

        LCM of 14 and 21 = 42

        \n\n

        ⇒ Total work = 42 units

        \n\n

        ⇒ A’s 1 hour work = 42 ÷ 14 = 3 units

        \n\n

        ⇒ B’s 1 hour work = 42 ÷ 21 = 2 units

        \n\n

        ⇒ (A + B)’s 1 hour work = 3 + 2 = 5 units

        \n\n

        Let B joins after x hours

        \n\n

        ⇒ Work by A alone = 3x

        \n\n

        ⇒ Remaining time = 10 − x hours

        \n\n

        ⇒ Work by A and B together = 5(10 − x)

        \n\n

        ⇒ 3x + 5(10 − x) = 42

        \n\n

        ⇒ 3x + 50 − 5x = 42

        \n\n

        ⇒ −2x = −8

        \n\n

        ⇒ x = 4 hours

        \n\n

        ∴ B should join A after 4 hours.

        \nc9:T816,\n

        दिया गया है:

        \n\n

        A किसी कार्य को 14 घंटे में कर सकता है

        \n\n

        B किसी कार्य को 21 घंटे में कर सकता है

        \n\n

        कुल समय = 10 घंटे

        \n\n
